boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's interrupt module (os_interrupt.c), 0x02056c40..0x02057014: 19 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt. Every member reads or writes the interrupt state: the handler table data_02099fe4, the DMA/timer callback table data_020a60c4 (timers from data_020a60f4), the IE-bit index table data_02099fd4, or IME/IE/IF (0x04000208/0x04000210/0x04000214).

mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order. Read from the highest address down, the run follows os_interrupt.c in order: OS_InitIrqTable (func_02057000), OS_SetIrqFunction (SetIRQHandler), OS_GetIrqFunction (GetIRQHandler), OSi_EnterDmaCallback (func_02056e98, IE bit 8+n), OSi_EnterTimerCallback (func_02056e4c, IE bit 3+n), OS_SetIrqMask, OS_EnableIrqMask, OS_DisableIrqMask, OS_ResetRequestIrqMask (ClearInterrupts), OS_IrqDummy (EmptyHandler), OSi_IrqCallback (DmaTimHandler), then the DMA 0-3 and timer 0-3 stubs.

TOP EDGE: func_02057014 at 0x02057014 is OS_UnLockCartridge, the bottom of OS_spinLock.c's run (its source documents OS_GetLockID/OS_ReleaseLockID at func_02057020/func_02057078 and OS_UnlockCartridge at func_02057178).
BOTTOM EDGE: Copy48BytesFixed at 0x02056c1c..0x02056c40 is a hand-assembled MI block-copy primitive, not interrupt code.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows arm9/GX_VramCnt.

Every existing linker name is kept: the IRQ:: members keep their namespace spelling, and the address-named members (func_02057000, func_02056e98, func_02056e4c) stay under extern "C" with the signatures their shards defined.
Text-only: the tables data_02099fe4, data_02099fd4 (.data) and data_020a60c4 (.bss) belong to this file in the SDK but are not claimed here.
PC port: smoke_gx hostgens func_02056e98 by symbol, which emits this whole file; everything else is under #ifndef _MSC_VER because port/ntr/runtime.cpp supplies the host interrupt registry.
